item.text: {"protocol_version":"wp5-v5","responses":[{"task_id":"risk-01-local-only-files","route":"guided","turns":[{"question":"Privacy boundary candidate. Recommendation: make this feature fully local for file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI, and telemetry. Reason: repository evidence shows derived text currently leaves the device and telemetry may leak excerpts. Impact: this defines the reversible slice and required controls. Evidence: remote AI provider receives derived text today; telemetry can include error payload excerpts; on-device parser supports the primary format. Uncertainty: non-primary formats may need later investigation. Reversibility: high, because the parser already runs on-device. Which privacy boundary should this feature enforce?","scripted_answer_index":0,"draft_ready":true}],"contract":{"G":"DECISION: local-only file processing; DECISION: file bytes, metadata, and derived text stay on-device, including AI and telemetry.","T":"DECISION: replace remote derived-text handling for this flow with on-device processing; DECISION: block telemetry from carrying file content or derived text.","S":"FACT: on-device parser supports the primary format; DECISION: reversible slice covers the primary format only; UNKNOWN: non-primary formats are non-blocking and out of scope.","V":"DECISION: verify no file bytes, metadata, or derived text leave the device; DECISION: verify telemetry/error paths contain no file content; DECISION: verify primary-format parsing still succeeds locally.","X":"DECISION: stop before adding remote AI, remote telemetry excerpts, or non-primary-format support.","P":"DECISION: no file-content persistence outside the device for this flow.","ready":true},"promotions":[],"stop_after_contract":true},{"task_id":"risk-03-data-retention","route":"guided","turns":[{"question":"Retention outcome candidate. Recommendation: delete uploads on a fixed schedule tied to report completion, while preserving the customer-visible artifact that still matters. Reason: uploads may still be referenced by completed reports, and no accepted retention policy exists. Impact: this sets the retention boundary for the reversible slice. Evidence: uploads may be referenced by completed reports; backups retain objects for 30 days; no accepted retention policy exists. Uncertainty: the exact retention window is not evidenced. Reversibility: high, because policy can be enforced as scheduled deletion. When should uploads be deleted relative to report completion, and what must remain available afterward?","scripted_answer_index":0,"draft_ready":false},{"question":"Recovery semantics candidate. Recommendation: tell users deletion is final in product behavior, while disaster-recovery backups age out separately and are not a user restore path. Reason: backups already retain objects for 30 days, so user-facing deletion semantics must be explicit. Impact: this closes the retention-control conflict. Evidence: backups retain objects for 30 days. Uncertainty: none material once the user-facing rule is chosen. Reversibility: medium, because wording and restore policy can later change with a policy revision. What should users be told about recovery after deletion while backups still exist for disaster recovery?","scripted_answer_index":1,"draft_ready":true}],"contract":{"G":"DECISION: automatically delete uploads 90 days after their last report finishes; DECISION: keep report summaries.","T":"DECISION: track each upload's last completed report finish time; DECISION: schedule deletion at day 90; DECISION: prevent completed reports from depending on deleted upload blobs.","S":"FACT: uploads may be referenced by completed reports; FACT: backups retain objects for 30 days; DECISION: reversible slice includes production deletion and user-facing final-deletion semantics, not backup redesign.","V":"DECISION: verify uploads delete 90 days after the last report finishes; DECISION: verify report summaries remain available after upload deletion; DECISION: verify user-facing messaging says deletion is final; DECISION: verify deleted uploads are not restorable through normal product flows.","X":"DECISION: stop before changing backup retention, restoring deleted uploads to users, or deleting report summaries.","P":"DECISION: persist summary records; FACT: disaster-recovery backups may retain deleted objects for 30 days; DECISION: product treats deletion as final despite backup aging.","ready":true},"promotions":[],"stop_after_contract":true},{"task_id":"risk-02-refund-authority","route":"guided","turns":[{"question":"Refund authority candidate. Recommendation: give support bounded refund authority with a required reason, and require stronger approval above that bound. Reason: support is currently read-only, and no approval threshold or audit event exists. Impact: this defines the authority boundary and mandatory control surface. Evidence: payment provider exposes full and partial refund APIs; support role currently has read-only billing access; no approval threshold or audit event exists. Uncertainty: the threshold amount is not evidenced. Reversibility: high, because limits and approver rules can be adjusted later. What refund authority should support have, and when is higher approval required?","scripted_answer_index":0,"draft_ready":false},{"question":"Refund shape candidate. Recommendation: allow partial refunds as well as full refunds within the approved support limit. Reason: the provider already supports both, and the remaining dependency is whether support needs both outcomes. Impact: this determines the executable refund paths in scope. Evidence: payment provider exposes full and partial refund APIs. Uncertainty: none material beyond the outcome choice. Reversibility: high, because narrower permissions can be reinstated later. Should support be able to issue partial refunds, full refunds, or both within that limit?","scripted_answer_index":1,"draft_ready":true}],"contract":{"G":"DECISION: support agents may refund up to $100 with a required reason; DECISION: larger refunds require an owner; DECISION: allow full and partial refunds within the support limit.","T":"DECISION: change support billing access from read-only to bounded refund authority; DECISION: require owner approval for refunds over $100; DECISION: record reason, actor, approver, amount, type, and provider refund id in an audit event.","S":"FACT: payment provider supports full and partial refunds; FACT: support role is read-only today; DECISION: reversible slice covers refund execution, approval gating, and audit evidence.","V":"DECISION: verify support can issue full or partial refunds up to $100 only with a reason; DECISION: verify refunds above $100 are blocked until owner approval exists; DECISION: verify every refund emits auditable approval and execution records.","X":"DECISION: stop before granting unlimited refund authority, removing required reasons, or processing over-limit refunds without owner approval.","P":"DECISION: persist immutable audit records for refund request, approval, and execution.","ready":true},"promotions":[],"stop_after_contract":true}]}
